answer: SybilRank stops fake clusters by measuring graph trust. A new identity enters at a supervised jetty portal, then must accumulate real interaction threads with established vertices. Random walks from trusted seeds spread rank: each vertex passes a fraction onward, so a sybil swarm's internal edges cannot mint trust, only dilute it. Cluster rank collapses below usefulness, keeping the swarm off every economic jetty. Attack cost: weeks of genuine history per accepted alias, making mass forgery uneconomical.
